person.name: Sreenath Pasupulati Kannaiah
person.title: Creative Designer
person.tagline: Turning good ideas into brands, motion and film people can't scroll past.
person.bio: I'm Sreenath Pasupulati Kannaiah, a creative designer based in Germany with over four years of experience creating brand identities, packaging, editorial systems, and visual campaigns. I believe the strongest design is built where strategy meets simplicity—work that solves problems, communicates clearly, and leaves a lasting impression. As my practice evolves, I'm expanding that same approach into motion graphics and video to create more complete brand experiences.
skills: Digital Marketing Creatives & Social Media Design

projects.title: VOID
projects.subtitle: Brand Identity
projects.blurb: A precision-engineered identity for a performance-wear system built on control, focus and relentless forward motion.

caseStudy.brief: VOID needed an identity that spoke to athletes who push beyond limits — not through noise, but through precision. The brand had to feel engineered, not decorated.
caseStudy.approach: The mark is built around a forward slash — a symbol of motion, direction and controlled energy — paired with a squared-off wordmark and a single acid-yellow accent against near-black. Every touchpoint, from transit takeovers to product tags, was built to whisper rather than shout.
caseStudy.result: A performance system where restraint becomes the loudest statement: “VOID isn't seen. It's felt.”

projects.title: Stratum
projects.subtitle: Packaging Design
projects.blurb: A monochrome packaging system for a skincare line, built around material honesty.

caseStudy.brief: Stratum needed packaging that felt clinical and premium at once — “where materials meet skin” — across four products (cleanser, serum, moisturizer, sunscreen) that had to read as one family from across a shelf.
caseStudy.approach: A restrained monochrome palette, textured matte surfaces and a strict numbering system (01–04) let the line read as a considered system rather than four separate SKUs, with German-language copy for the target market.
caseStudy.result: A quiet, tactile packaging suite that lets texture and typography carry the premium feel instead of color or ornament.

projects.title: Origin 83
projects.subtitle: Coffee Branding
projects.blurb: A single-origin coffee brand inspired by the landscapes and tribal heritage of Araku Valley, India.

caseStudy.brief: Origin 83 — named for the 83° East longitude running through Araku Valley — needed an identity that honored the region's indigenous coffee-growing heritage without resorting to cliche “rustic” branding.
caseStudy.approach: A mark built from the valley's mountain silhouette, a curated palette (Ivory, Valley Blue, Origin Gold, Tribal Land) drawn directly from the landscape and tribal textiles, and editorial-weight serif type carry the story across pod packaging, bags and collateral.
caseStudy.result: “Brewed through generations” — a brand that reads as heritage-led rather than decorative, rooted in a specific place and its people.

projects.title: Bunny
projects.subtitle: AI Brand Identity
projects.blurb: A sculptural, quiet identity for an AI companion built around presence rather than spectacle.

caseStudy.brief: Bunny is an AI companion positioned around “quiet intelligence” — the brand needed to feel calm and present, not like another loud AI product chasing attention.
caseStudy.approach: A soft sculptural mark — a continuous form suggesting two rounded ears — sits over a moss-and-cream palette, paired with a serif/sans pairing that lets the product feel considered rather than clinical, extended into a full marketing site.
caseStudy.result: “Quiet Intelligence. Always by your side.” — an identity that stands apart from typical AI branding by choosing restraint over spectacle.

projects.title: Making
projects.subtitle: Editorial Design
projects.blurb: A conceptual editorial magazine exploring how design and material honesty shape tomorrow's world.

caseStudy.brief: MAKING is a self-directed editorial project — each issue built around a single guiding question about design and culture. Issue 02 asks: “How do today's designers shape tomorrow's world?”
caseStudy.approach: An organic blob-shaped graphic system contrasts with a disciplined editorial grid; the issue explores its theme through the lens of material honesty — timber, stone, paper, concrete — using full-bleed photography and restrained serif/sans typography.
caseStudy.result: A cohesive editorial identity that treats the magazine itself as a design object, not just a container for articles.
